description: Write or draw the supplied color-aware reference with physical markers.
count_scope: 10,000 native variations and seven fixed task presets

evaluator.scope: Environment-owned task success; not physical qualification.

qualification: Defined task catalogue; does not imply every variation passed physical qualification.

task_set_v1.score_rule: 1 on success, otherwise 0.9 x continuous progress; untouched starts score zero
task_set_v1.legacy: Omitted selection and all native variation/split/kind/selection_seed requests use the native resolver. Named presets require their explicit contract.
task_set_v1.launch: Resolve with GAR tasks and launch its LaunchSpec/TaskSpec (including saved manifests and managed sessions), or construct NewtonWhiteboardTaskSetBackend directly. The registry factory creates native whiteboard sessions only.
task_set_v1.qualification: Checked by constructed-state unit tests only; the seven presets have not been run with the simulator or rendered.

task_set.note: The render-checked set (each of the eight untouched starts starts, renders and scores 0). Same seven named presets and native bridge as task_set_v1, with the same authored starts, instructions, verifiers, progress and score. What differs from v1: the contract (whiteboard-tasks-v2, in task ids, backend options and every evaluation), draw-table reports its contract unsuffixed like every task (its table metric is labelled whiteboard-tasks-v2/draw-table), and task_source_sha256 also covers whiteboard/task_set_v2.py and task_set_v2_backend.py. Adding v2 also changes the task_source_sha256 that task_set_v1 runs report (7837e2a2... in the release), because that hash covers benchmark.json, task_set/catalogue.py and the task-set backend, which gained the v2 entry; the v1 starts, instructions, verifiers, progress and scores are unchanged. The bridge keeps its native test-split selection (variation_id 0) and bridge-copy-v1.
